                                  PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

 JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR                  §

 CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY                   §
 FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST                    §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION               §
 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE                    §
 PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,                    §
 CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                  §      OF
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH,                    §
 MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN                   §
 SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                §      TEXAS
 AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                     §


     CITY OF BRADY TEXAS’ TESTIMONY BY CITY MANAGER JAMES STEWART


                                           I.
                                     INTRODUCTION

Q: Please state your name for the record.

A: JAMES STEWART

Q: What is your address?

A:      Business address:
        City of Brady
        201 E Main Street
        Brady, Texas, 76825

Q: Have you ever testified in a Public Utility Commission of Texas (“PUC” or “Commission”)
proceeding?

A: No


Q: Are you an intervenor in “PUC Docket No. 59475, SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349—
JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA
TSC TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE



                                            Stewart Testimony 59475, CITY OF BRADY, Page 1 of 6
   59475 - EXHIBIT 1 - CITY OF BRADY - STEWART TESTIMONY - PAGE 002 OF 6



BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION
LINE PROJECT”, and on whose behalf are you testifying?

A: Yes, I am the representative of intervenor, City of Brady. As such, I am testifying on behalf of
the City of Brady as its City Manager as an entity and on behalf of the residents therein.


                                      II.
                        PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF TESTIMONY

Q: What is the purpose of your testimony?

A: To testify about the City of Brady’s concerns with and objections to this project and the
proposed Link V8 that is less than 20,000 feet from the City’s Curtis Field Airport, and why this
proposed route should not be used.

Q: Are you familiar with the Study Area as described by Applicant’s Application, and if yes,
please explain?

A: Yes, I am familiar with this Phase one of the project, and the routes that are being considered.
Of the 122 alternative routes, using Link V8 is unnecessary and does not best conform to criteria
because there are other proposed routes which are flatter, straighter and provide a more direct east-
west route without unnecessarily making a sharp north detour to get to the west end-point.

Q: Where are your properties located?

A: The City of Brady does not bear any Oncor Interactive Numbers but the City’s airport is less
than 20,000 feet from Link V8 south of Oncor Interactive Number 4236 (see attached Exhibit 1)


                                       III.
                          Description Of Your Property
        And Your Concerns About The Project Relative To It And To The Area.

Q: What Links impact your properties and explain how they do so.

A: The link that impacts City of Brady is V8.

•       V8 does not consider some of the Key factors and justifications the PUC considers valid for
selecting a transmission line route including:




                                                Stewart Testimony 59475, CITY OF BRADY, Page 2 of 6
      59475 - EXHIBIT 1 - CITY OF BRADY - STEWART TESTIMONY - PAGE 003 OF 6



                •   Utilization of Existing Rights-of-Way:

                        o   V8 does not appear to follow existing rights of way and crosses private farm
                            land which disrupts new land properties.

                •   Property Line Following:

                        o   V8 fragments agricultural land and large parcels of land and does not follow
                            existing property lines.

                •   "Prudent Avoidance" Policy: The commission evaluates routes based on "prudent
                    avoidance," which means taking reasonable, low-cost steps to limit exposure to
                    electric and magnetic fields (EMF).

                •   Community Values and Aesthetics:

                        o   V8 goes down large residential and farm land areas.

                •   Uncontested/Settlement Routes:

                        o   V8 appears to be a very gerrymandered link. V8 land owners are also
                            opposed and have a right to not have their farm land, homes and aquifers
                            disrupted.

        a. V8 poses a potentially significant impact on the future expansion of the Curtis Field Airport.
           Curtis Field is located approximately less than sixteen thousand feet south of where the V8
           line would cross and any further lengthening of the runway would have a direct impact on the
           flight path requirements which would be negatively impacted by a transmission line of the
           height of the proposed 765kV line. Our community is continually looking for ways to expand
           its economic base due to our rural location and increasing our airport’s capabilities by adding
           500 feet more in length would make a significant impact to the airport’s ability to accept a
           wider variety of planes.



Q: Are there any issues with Link V8 in general that you believe should be addressed by the
commission?

A:      Yes.

        a. Gerrymandered V8 Link: The proposed middle routes for the power line in question
           basically run east-west with the exception of some routes which for some reason offer
           gerrymandered routes. Link V8 would basically be a severe north-south “detour” from
           one proposed route to another. There appears to be no rational basis to use this detoured
           route instead of using a more central straight-line east-west route which should be the
           shortest distance for this power line. The detour created by proposed Line V8 should
           not be considered as an alternate route. Using Link V8 could greatly impact Brady’s
           economic growth by limiting its airport use and expansion.


                                                     Stewart Testimony 59475, CITY OF BRADY, Page 3 of 6
   59475 - EXHIBIT 1 - CITY OF BRADY - STEWART TESTIMONY - PAGE 004 OF 6




       b. Please also see response to the immediately preceding question.

Q: Are there any issues with any other links that you believe should be addressed by the
commission?

A: Yes.
   a. All the links are concerning as there has been little information that I have seen regarding
       alternatives such as nuclear power, natural gas power or other alternatives that would not
       necessitate such a large line across Texas.

   b. Oncor/LCRA’s contention that there is a public purpose of a utility seems to be an
      overstretch and unreasonable and unnecessary attempt at taking private property with this
      much infrastructure. Are we trying to promote the GRID not failing again or helping private
      companies that should be pursuing alternative energy?

       If there is ultimately a determination by the PUC that this power line is necessary and serves
       a public purpose, then Oncor/LCRA should be compelled to locate the power line (a) using
       the most direct route and (b) locate the line in areas with the least negative impact on private
       property.

Q: Please tell the Commissioners about the history of your property.

A: The City of Brady is a home rule municipality in McCulloch County that has a small airport
and mostly rural activities across V8.


Q: What activities occur on your property?

A: Municipality with adjacent Airport .

Q: Please describe your property’s terrain and ecological features.

A: The terrain is flat and has been in use as a municipal airport for the past 50 years.

Q: Would constructing this transmission line on any of the proposed Links conflict with
community values in our area, recreations /park areas and or any cultural/historic sites.

A: Yes. Families are relocating to this area because of quality of life here and educational
opportunities for their children as well as the aesthetic value of rural Texas. A significant number
of families that have deep roots in the area are concerned with the negative impact an unsightly
transmission line might have on the value of their property. Additionally the size alone of the line
could hinder our airport.


                                                  Stewart Testimony 59475, CITY OF BRADY, Page 4 of 6
   59475 - EXHIBIT 1 - CITY OF BRADY - STEWART TESTIMONY - PAGE 005 OF 6




                                           IV.
                             Conclusion and Recommendations

Q: How would you summarize your position in this proceeding regarding routing?

A: I believe that the proposed routing should follow a path along either a previously established
right of way in order to minimize the impact on private landowners and I think that the
gerrymandered V8 link would have a negative impact on the future economic growth potential
related to the future plans to expand and lengthen the runway of Curtis Field. The airport is a vital
link to the rest of the state and beyond as it brings in outside commerce and trade that directly
impacts our local economy. Coupled with the negative impact it would have on property values, I
recommend the PUC consider alternative routing.


Q: Does this conclude your testimony?

A: Yes

END OF TESTIMONY


                                UNSWORN DECLARATION

       My name is JAMES STEWART. My date of birth is 06/29/1970, and my address is City
Manager, City of Brady, 201 E Main Street, Brady, Texas, 76825. I hereby declare under
penalty of perjury that the foregoing Direct Testimony is true and correct.”

         Executed this 13th day of May 2026 in Brady, McCulloch County Texas.
